meta.title: The Connected Homage: Your AI Integration Roadmap
meta.subtitle: From Celigo to a platform your team owns — and an inventory intelligence layer that watches for you

challenge.lead: You're evaluating three or four vendors, and the right question is not 'who builds MuleSoft flows' — everyone does. The right question is: who already knows how Celigo is built on the inside, before you show them anything? Celigo's Standard Integration App doesn't create one flow per category — it creates separate flows per direction and per CRUD operation. That's why your 10 briefing categories are actually 23 flows. We named 18 of them from your document before this call. That's not preparation — that's the pattern knowledge that determines whether your migration lands in 35 weeks or drags to 50.

cards.label: Your Integration Layer Is Third-Party Owned
cards.text: Sikich manages your Celigo day-to-day — monitoring, changes, fixes. Every integration incident, every custom JavaScript update, every ad-hoc mapping correction runs through your NetSuite partner. That operational dependency ends on go-live day.

cards.label: 23 Flows, Custom JS, No Single Owner
cards.text: Your Celigo footprint runs one Standard Integration App plus three custom integrations — ~23 flows, many with pre-map, post-response, and post-submit JavaScript hooks that only Sikich fully understands. When that institutional knowledge is unavailable, the logic is at risk.

cards.label: Two Integration Tracks Running Outside Celigo
cards.text: Your Orderful EDI track (810/856/997 with Fanatics, DSG, and Rallyhouse) and your ShipStation connection via Turbine both run outside Celigo today. Two critical operational tracks with no unified integration owner — and no single monitoring surface.

solution.lead: MuleSoft replaces the Celigo + Turbine + custom JavaScript layer with a single DataSkate-managed integration platform. Unlike native marketplace connectors, MuleSoft adds retry logic, dead letter queues, idempotency checks, and a live operations layer — so when Shopify fires a webhook at 2am on Cyber Monday, the order lands in NetSuite and someone is watching.
solution.diagramCaption: DataSkate-managed MuleSoft layer — no code changes required in Shopify Plus or NetSuite

roi.headline: The business case for moving now
roi.body: Homage's 22 confirmed Celigo flows represent the primary migration scope — 17 individually named, 5 awaiting the Celigo flow inventory spreadsheet. The custom JavaScript transforms embedded across those flows are the #1 source of migration cost overruns industry-wide: each one is a business rule that lives in Sikich's memory and in the code. Topo Designs — the same Shopify + NetSuite stack, mid-market apparel — eliminated two admin roles and compressed month-end close to 5 days after their migration. A Fortune 500 retailer using MuleSoft went from 7–10 days of manual inventory coordination to under 1 hour and recovered $3.8M per quarter in markdown losses.

journey.headline: the path to a clear picture of platform fit for your stack — NetSuite, Shopify, and EDI all connected, reliable, and owned by you

stage1.label: Connected
stage1.headline: All 22 Celigo flows live on MuleSoft — DataSkate-owned, monitored, and under one operational surface
items: Sikich's Celigo monitoring call stops on go-live day — DataSkate owns the integration layer
Every order placed on homage.com creates a cash sale or sales order in NetSuite immediately, routing logic applied automatically
Inventory levels — including CSWOS tiered thresholds — sync from NetSuite to Shopify in near-real-time, no manual toggle per SKU
Matrix item price and tax changes in NetSuite propagate to Shopify within minutes — no spreadsheet, no delay
Fulfillments write back automatically; returns from Shopify reconcile to NetSuite without a manual correction cycle
Custom JS hooks replaced by documented DataWeave transforms — the logic is ours to maintain, not Sikich's to patch

stage2.label: Automated
stage2.headline: NetSuite inventory and EDI demand signals drive Shopify merchandising automatically
items: NetSuite inventory drops below a threshold → Shopify applies CSWOS rules for that SKU automatically — no human toggle
EDI purchase order from Fanatics or DSG arrives → NetSuite checks available inventory and flags fulfillment risk before the acknowledgment is sent
Matrix item price changes in NetSuite propagate to Shopify within minutes — no manual step between ERP and storefront
Month-end financial close shrinks: billing transactions, customer deposits, and invoice transformations run without human touch

stage3.label: Agentic
stage3.headline: An AI agent monitors every SKU's velocity, EDI demand, and restock lead time — surfacing margin risk before the fulfillment window closes
items: Which SKUs are at risk of missing a Fanatics or DSG fulfillment window in the next 72 hours — and what specifically should we do about it?

When sales velocity plus open EDI demand plus restock lead time signal a stockout risk, the agent surfaces the specific action: apply CSWOS, restrict EDI allocation, request emergency restock, or initiate a markdown

No spreadsheet. No Monday morning surprise. The data it reads — order intake, inventory levels, fulfillment events, EDI demand from Orderful — is built in Stage 1. Without Stage 1, this question is unanswerable.

journey.closingLine: Stage 1 eliminates the specific manual work your team does today. Stages 2 and 3 build on that foundation — but the immediate win is on go-live day.

flows.name: Shopify Order → NetSuite Cash Sale
flows.value: Every DTC order on homage.com creates a cash sale in NetSuite on payment — no manual entry, no lag between storefront and ERP.

flows.name: Shopify Order → NetSuite Sales Order
flows.value: B2B and net-terms orders route to NetSuite as sales orders, not cash sales — classification logic applied automatically, no manual routing decision.

flows.name: Shopify Refund → NetSuite Credit Memo / Customer Refund
flows.value: Shopify refunds create the correct NetSuite record automatically — credit memo or customer refund — without a reconciliation queue or manual match.

flows.name: NetSuite Return Authorization → Shopify Refund
flows.value: Return authorizations created in NetSuite trigger the corresponding Shopify refund automatically — both systems stay in sync without manual matching.

flows.name: NetSuite Item Fulfillment → Shopify Fulfillment Update
flows.value: When a fulfillment ships in NetSuite, tracking numbers write back to Shopify instantly — customers receive accurate shipping status without a manual update.

flows.name: Shopify Fulfillment Event → NetSuite Order Status
flows.value: Shopify fulfillment events update NetSuite sales order status automatically — ops knows what shipped without checking two systems.

flows.name: Inventory Sync (Scheduled + CSWOS Logic)
flows.value: NetSuite inventory levels sync to Shopify on schedule, including CSWOS tiered thresholds per SKU — no manual toggle required when stock drops below a threshold.

flows.name: NetSuite Matrix Item → Shopify Product + Variants
flows.value: Matrix item updates in NetSuite propagate to Shopify products and variants automatically — the product catalog stays current without re-entry in Shopify.

flows.name: NetSuite Price → Shopify Product Price
flows.value: Price changes in NetSuite push to Shopify variant pricing — no spreadsheet, no delay, no price discrepancy between ERP and storefront.

flows.name: NetSuite Tax Code → Shopify Product Tax
flows.value: Tax schedule changes in NetSuite update Shopify taxable settings automatically — compliance is handled without a manual configuration step.

flows.name: Shopify Product Image URL → NetSuite Item
flows.value: Product images updated in Shopify write back to NetSuite item records — catalog data stays synchronized across both platforms.

flows.name: Shopify Customer Created → NetSuite Customer
flows.value: New Shopify customers create NetSuite customer records with deduplication logic — no duplicate records, no manual lookup required.

flows.name: Shopify Customer Updated → NetSuite Customer
flows.value: Customer updates in Shopify propagate to NetSuite — contact and billing data stays current in the ERP without manual data entry.

flows.name: NetSuite Customer → Shopify Customer
flows.value: Customer updates in NetSuite write back to Shopify — with loop-prevention logic to avoid circular sync between the two systems.

flows.name: Shopify Payment → NetSuite Customer Deposit
flows.value: Shopify payment settlement creates NetSuite customer deposit records automatically — billing reconciliation runs itself without a manual step.

flows.name: NetSuite Sales Order → Invoice Trigger
flows.value: Sales orders reaching billing-eligible status trigger the NetSuite invoice workflow — internal automation with no external dependency.

flows.name: Shopify Store Metadata → NetSuite Custom Records
flows.value: Shopify store metadata changes update the corresponding NetSuite custom records automatically — operational data stays synchronized.

outcomes.title: Operational Independence
outcomes.body: Your integration layer moves from Sikich-managed to DataSkate-owned. Monitoring, incident response, and day-to-day changes no longer route through your NetSuite partner.

outcomes.title: Inventory on Autopilot
outcomes.body: NetSuite inventory levels, CSWOS thresholds, matrix item pricing, and EDI demand signals sync automatically — no manual SKU-level toggles, no spreadsheet-based inventory reviews.

outcomes.title: AI-Ready Foundation
outcomes.body: Clean, connected, well-maintained data infrastructure is what AI agents need to operate. Every flow we build is a pipeline an AI agent will eventually use — built right from the start.

oos.title: NetSuite configuration & SuiteScript
oos.detail: Custom record type creation, chart of accounts changes, SuiteScript development, and all Sikich-managed NetSuite administration are out of scope.

oos.title: Shopify theme & storefront development
oos.detail: Storefront customization, Shopify app development, Shopify Payments configuration, and theme changes are out of scope.

oos.title: Historical data migration
oos.detail: This engagement covers net-new data flowing from go-live forward. Historical Celigo flow records and legacy transactional data are not migrated.

oos.title: Celigo decommission
oos.detail: Celigo account termination, credential revocation, and Sikich handoff coordination are client responsibilities.

oos.title: Orderful & ShipStation account setup
oos.detail: Trading partner EDI mapping, Orderful portal configuration, carrier setup, and Turbine logic documentation are client and partner responsibilities before DataSkate build begins.

oos.title: Adjacent expansion flows (UC14–UC18)
oos.detail: ShipStation tracking writeback, Loop Returns reconciliation, and three Orderful EDI flows (inbound PO, outbound ASN, outbound Invoice) are identified but not priced in this proposal. Ready to scope on request.
